gap: No result ChatGPT got states today's maker-store prices across the category: Samsung's US business store lists the Galaxy Tab Active5 Pro at $759 (Wi-Fi, 128 GB) and $869 (5G); Panasonic and Getac publish no price and ask buyers to request a quote; Dell's US page marks the Latitude 7030 Rugged Extreme 'Unavailable'; and Blackview's own store sells the IP68/IP69K Active 8 Pro at $289 and the Active 10 Pro at $375.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Panasonic G2 pages (connect.na.panasonic.com and eu.connect.panasonic.com, neither shows a price) and itechguides.com, which ranks in the top results (read 2026-11-14). itechguides gives Tab Active5 Pro $659.00 and Tab Active5 $499.99 as a 'dated US price capture'. Its Dell prices ($2,552.04 for the 7030, $3,030.31 for the 7230) are 2024 Principled Technologies test configurations. It names the Getac ZX10, not the UX10. No rival page prices Blackview, says the 7030 is no longer sold on Dell US, or notes that Samsung's own 5G price ($869) is above the Newegg card ChatGPT showed ($775.70). rottenwifi.com timed out twice and was not read.
decides: It confirms that the choice splits by OS and price. The Windows tablets with a 1,000-nit screen and a 6 ft drop rating (Panasonic G2 MK3, Getac UX10) are sold by quote, and ChatGPT's own cards show them at about $3,500 to $3,800. Samsung's own store puts the Tab Active5 Pro at $759 to $869. Blackview's store sells our Active 10 Pro for half of that ($375). The Latitude 7030 should come off the list because Dell US shows it as unavailable. The Blackview price would change the budget pick only if its display brightness and enterprise support can be sourced, and they were not.
